descriptors.concept_name: Roadmap For Applicability Of Ind As
descriptors.definition: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs mandates a structured, phased transition framework for implementing Indian Accounting Standards across eligible corporate entities. This roadmap outlines specific applicability timelines and net worth criteria for listed and unlisted entities while excluding banking and insurance companies.
inclusion: Listed companies meeting net worth thresholds
Unlisted companies meeting specific net worth limits
Holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate entities of covered companies
exclusion: Banking companies
Insurance companies
Companies listed on SME exchanges or Institutional Trading Platforms
nearby_distinctions: Differs from NBFC-specific phased roadmaps by applying general corporate thresholds rather than specialized financial sector criteria.

descriptors.definition: Listed entities are subjected to mandatory Ind AS adoption through a two-tier phased timeline determined by their security listing status and net worth thresholds. Phase I covers entities with a net worth of rupees five hundred crore or more, whereas Phase II captures those with lower net worth values.
inclusion: Entities with equity or debt securities listed on Indian or foreign stock exchanges
Entities in the process of listing their securities
exclusion: Entities listed exclusively on SME exchanges
Entities listed on Institutional Trading Platforms without an initial public offering
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from unlisted entities by lower net worth entry barriers under Phase II.

descriptors.concept_name: Ind As Roadmap For Non -Banking Financial Companies (Nbfc)
descriptors.definition: Non-banking financial companies follow a distinct two-phase transition timeline for adopting Indian Accounting Standards based on specified net worth brackets and listing attributes. The framework encompasses diverse financial entities such as housing finance companies, microfinance institutions, and core investment companies.
inclusion: Housing finance companies
Micro finance companies
Core investment companies
NBFCs with net worth of 500 crores or more
exclusion: Non-financial companies under the primary corporate roadmap
NBFCs with net worth below two hundred and fifty crores not meeting listing criteria
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard corporate timelines by incorporating financial sector entities under modified asset and listing parameters.

descriptors.concept_name: Ind As Roadmap For Banking And Insurance Companies
descriptors.definition: Banking and insurance entities are currently exempted from applying Indian Accounting Standards until such standards are formally notified by their respective sectoral regulators. Furthermore, voluntary adoption of Ind AS is strictly prohibited for these specific institutional sectors.
inclusion: Banking companies governed by RBI
Insurance companies governed by IRDA
exclusion: Non-banking corporate entities
Mutual funds operating under separate market regulations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general corporate entities and NBFCs because statutory timelines depend entirely on direct sector-specific regulatory notifications rather than Ministry of Corporate Affairs phases.

descriptors.concept_name: Ind As Roadmap For Mutual Funds
descriptors.definition: Mutual fund schemes are mandated to prepare their financial statements and accounts in compliance with Indian Accounting Standards pursuant to specific regulatory amendments. This operational shift enhances transparency and aligns scheme accounting frameworks with prescribed format guidelines.
inclusion: Mutual fund operational schemes
Financial accounts governed by market regulatory amendments
exclusion: Standard corporate entities under general manufacturing or service roadmaps
Banking and insurance institutions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from corporate entities by deriving its implementation mandate directly from market regulator guidelines rather than standard company law thresholds.

descriptors.definition: Primary statutory provisions embedded within company legislation govern the definition, adoption, auditing, and corporate compliance of accounting standards. These provisions dictate mandatory inclusions for financial statement presentation, directors' responsibility statements, auditor reports, and corporate restructuring schemes.
inclusion: Financial statement compliance declarations
Auditor opinions on accounting standards
Scheme of arrangement conformity certificates
exclusion: Non-statutory voluntary disclosures lacking legal backing
Informal management reporting frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general accounting guidelines by carrying direct penal and legal consequences under company law for non-compliance.

descriptors.concept_name: Relevant Sections Referring To Ind As In The Companies Act, 2013 And Rules
descriptors.definition: Key sections of the primary company statute govern the legal recognition and application of accounting standards, including prescriptions by the Central Government and recommendations by regulatory bodies. These legal references control financial statement disclosures, audit verifications, capital reductions, and corporate mergers.
inclusion: Central Government prescribing standards in consultation with NFRA
Tribunal sanction requirements for capital reductions and amalgamations
exclusion: Unregulated internal accounting policies
Standards formulated outside statutory consultative frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Differs from secondary rules by forming the primary legislative authority empowering the notification of specific accounting frameworks.

descriptors.definition: Capital market regulatory guidelines require listed entities adopting new accounting frameworks to ensure that all submitted periodic financial results and comparative figures are fully compliant. Additionally, these rules dictate the financial history disclosure requirements within public offer documents.
inclusion: Comparative quarterly and annual financial statements
Multi-year financial disclosures in public issue offer documents
exclusion: Unlisted companies exempt from market regulator oversight
Internal management reports not submitted to stock exchanges
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general company law mandates by imposing strict capital market disclosure timelines and filing formats.

descriptors.concept_name: Format Of Division II To Schedule III To The Companies Act - Structure
descriptors.definition: Division II prescribes the mandatory financial statement presentation format for companies required to comply with Indian Accounting Standards. The structure categorizes reporting into balance sheet elements, statement of profit and loss items, and general instructions for consolidated financial statements.
inclusion: Balance sheet and statement of changes in equity format
Statement of profit and loss format
General instructions for consolidated financial statements
exclusion: Insurance and banking companies
Non-banking financial companies utilizing Division III formats
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Division I and Division III formats by being exclusively tailored for non-banking entities adopting Ind AS.

descriptors.definition: Schedule III establishes the statutory presentation structure for financial statements prepared by companies registered under corporate legislation. Financial statements prepared under this framework encompass balance sheets, equity change statements, profit and loss statements, cash flow statements, and explanatory notes.
inclusion: Balance sheet and profit and loss statements
Cash flow statements and statements of changes in equity
exclusion: Schedules governed entirely by separate legislative acts for specialized financial sectors
Informal financial summaries
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from individual accounting standards by focusing strictly on presentation layout and disclosure structures rather than recognition and measurement rules.

descriptors.definition: Schedule III presentation rules apply to all companies preparing financial statements in compliance with corporate accounting rules, supported by specialized guidance notes and regulatory circulars. Preparers must incorporate amendments introduced to presentation requirements for financial years commencing on or after specified dates.
inclusion: Mandatory Ind AS compliant companies
Voluntary Ind AS compliant companies
exclusion: Entities exempted under specific statutory sector rules
Non-corporate business entities
nearby_distinctions: Differs from initial standard-setting notifications by establishing the ongoing annual presentation framework for active financial reporting.

descriptors.concept_name: Guidance Note On Division II To Schedule III To The Companies Act, 2013
descriptors.definition: The professional institute issues implementation guidance to resolve practical compliance issues arising from the application of financial statement formats for companies under Indian Accounting Standards. This guidance mandates specific classifications, such as presenting land and building as separate asset classes and isolating capital advances under non-current assets.
inclusion: Separate classification of land and building
Presentation of capital advances under other non-current assets
Sub-classification disclosures for subsidiary and associate investments
exclusion: Grouping land and building together for revaluation purposes under operational standard rules
Including capital advances within capital work-in-progress
nearby_distinctions: Differs from baseline standard texts by enforcing strict schedule layout presentations that override generalized grouping permissions found in specific accounting standards.
